source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Interpret the findings as a routine extrapyramidal effect and continue the current antipsychotic while monitoring at the usual interval.","B":"Interpret the findings as an uncomplicated viral illness because severe rigidity and autonomic instability are not associated with haloperidol.","C":"Suspect neuroleptic malignant syndrome, stop the causative antipsychotic, and obtain urgent supportive treatment and medical monitoring.","D":"Interpret the findings as a benign expected medication effect because fever and autonomic instability do not require urgent evaluation."}}
source_row.rationale: Haloperidol labeling identifies neuroleptic malignant syndrome as a potentially fatal syndrome characterized by hyperpyrexia, muscle rigidity, altered mental status, and autonomic instability. Option C is correct because management includes immediate discontinuation of antipsychotic drugs with intensive symptomatic treatment and monitoring. Option A dangerously normalizes the syndrome as routine EPS. Option B incorrectly excludes a medication-related emergency. Option D incorrectly treats the presentation as benign.
source_row.source_detail: DailyMed Haloperidol Tablets — Warnings, Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome: potentially fatal NMS includes hyperpyrexia, muscle rigidity, altered mental status, and autonomic instability; management includes immediate discontinuation of antipsychotic drugs plus intensive symptomatic treatment and medical monitoring. FDA haloperidol tablets label updated 2025-01-28; current DailyMed label live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: medication routes, administration, reversal, adverse effects/interactions, withdrawal, monitoring and client teaching. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
source_row.stem: A client taking haloperidol develops high fever, severe muscle rigidity, altered mental status, and autonomic instability. Which interpretation is most appropriate?
